transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I wanted to convene this group because we have a deficiency letter from the regulator regarding our pediatric monitoring device, and our written response is due in 30 calendar days. We have a draft response circulating internally, but it has not been approved or submitted yet. The draft still leaves several critical questions unresolved — specifically around the device's software scope, lot disposition, the pediatric indication, and the patient-data fields to be included. We need to get alignment on these open items so we can finalize and submit a defensible response within the deadline. I'd like to hear from each of you on where things stand in your respective areas.

After our last technical call with the regulator, I received a written follow-up from them that places two specific constraints on our response: first, the response must be limited to software version 4.2, and second, it must include an answer matrix with exactly six question rows. I saved that message in the regulatory mailbox, but I have not yet incorporated these requirements into the circulated draft. We need to make sure the final response complies with both of these directives.

transcript.text: I need to share something critical from my latest quality-audit packet review. During the audit, we identified calibration deviations in lots L17 and L18. These two lots must be placed on hold and fully investigated before any release. This finding has not yet been added to the corrective-action section of the circulated draft response. Given that the draft already has unresolved questions about lot disposition, we need to address this — the regulator asked about manufacturing controls, and releasing or referencing these lots without proper disposition and investigation would be a significant compliance issue.
